articles.headline: DFWGilly Takes the Shart in Week 3
articles.deck: Lowest score of the week, 50.56 points.
body: Romo911 scored 50.56 in Week 3, the lowest total in the league.
jwslaney took the win.
That is a chug. The rules are the rules.

articles.headline: The Week 3 Hardware
body: Manager of the Week: Andrew, Bibi’s Ballers 69, 151.64 points.
The Shart: Aaron, Romo911, 50.56 points.
Blowout: Josef, Zyn-bo Squisher, won by 53.58.
Squeaker: John, BedBathNBIJAN22, won by 4.74.
Lucky Dog: Jack, Cook’d, won with 94.76.
Heartbreaker: Adam, First Down Syndrome, lost with 135.04.
Bench Rot: Sean, Burrowed Alive, 57.78 on the bench.

articles.headline: Andrew Drops 151.64 And Still Can't Buy A Winning Record
articles.deck: Bibi's Ballers 69 put up the week's biggest number, Jahmyr Gibbs went nuclear, and somehow the man still looks up at half the league in the standings.
body: Let's give credit where it's due. Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 dropped 151.64 on Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, the loudest number anybody posted in Week 3, and he did it behind Jahmyr Gibbs going off for 41.4 points, the single best performance in the entire league this week. That is not a system score. That is a nuke.

Jeff, for what it's worth, did not exactly lay down. Chase Browns with Downs put up 130.54 and still got run over, because Drake London chipped in 28.4 for him and it simply wasn't enough against a runaway Lions back. Margin ended at 21.1. Some weeks you just get outgunned.

Now the undercut, because this is the SquirtRag and we don't let anybody walk out of here feeling too good about himself. Bibi's Ballers 69 sits at 1-2 on the season with a 47 percent shot at the playoffs, tagged Bubble, staring up at teams like Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy and 50 Shades of Zay who haven't lost yet. You can score 151.64 in a week and it still just gets you to 1-2 if your first two weeks were a dumpster fire. Andrew, this is your reminder that Gibbs can't play every week for you and neither can your sense of timing. Great week. Rough season so far. Both things are true.

articles.headline: BedBathNBIJAN22 Survives Bijan Bowl By 4.74
articles.deck: John and Adam turned Week 3 into a shootout, and one lousy field goal's worth of points decided who leaves happy.
body: This was the only game all week that deserved a hype trailer, and it delivered. First Down Syndrome's Adam put up 135.04, the kind of number that wins most weeks in this league, and walked away with nothing to show for it but a Heartbreaker trophy and a long car ride home.

John's BedBathNBIJAN22 squad matched him blow for blow behind Bijan Robinson going for 35.3 and Brock Purdy chipping in 31.28 through the air. That's two guys doing the heavy lifting while the rest of the roster just had to not screw it up, and for once, nobody screwed it up.

On the other side, Adam's Jaxon Smith-Njigba dropped 35.36, the single best receiver performance anybody put up this week, and it still wasn't enough. That's the cruelty of this league in a sentence: you can have the top guy at his position and still watch the scoreboard turn on you like a bad Tinder date.

139.78 to 135.04. That's it. That's the whole margin, 4.74 points, closer than anything else on the slate this week, closer than a Zoom call with your ex. Adam gets to walk into Week 4 against Romo911 knowing he did nothing wrong and lost anyway, which might be worse than getting blown out. John gets to walk into a date with nunnells at 3-0 feeling like a genius, right up until the next Sunday reminds him nobody's a genius in this league for long.

articles.headline: Around The League Week 3 Nobody Was Safe
articles.deck: Six matchups, six different flavors of suffering, and one commissioner who got to watch all of it happen from a safe distance.
body: Jackson Off put up 135.44 and buried Victorious Secrets 107.58, and Taylor drops to 0-3 while everyone in the group chat pretends not to notice. Ben got 27.6 out of Brock Bowers and didn't even need it, which is the fantasy football equivalent of overkill on a parking ticket.

Cook'd scraped by Burrowed Alive 94.76 to 71.58, a game that felt less like a fantasy matchup and more like watching two guys argue over who gets the smaller piece of cake. Sean falls to 0-3 and is now staring up at the entire league from the basement.

50 Shades of Zay did not play a close game, they played a public execution, dropping 141.08 on Hog tied and deep fried's 95.06 for a 46.02 margin. Trip sits at 3-0 and leads the league in points for, and at this point somebody should check his roster for a hidden thirteenth man.

Bibi's Ballers 69 outlasted Chase Browns with Downs 151.64 to 130.54 in the highest scoring loss of the week, because Jahmyr Gibbs decided to have a 41.4 point fever dream. Jeff got 28.4 from Drake London and it still wasn't enough, which tells you everything about how absurd Andrew's afternoon was.

Zyn-bo Squisher stomped Romo911 by a 53.58 margin, 104.14 to 50.56, and Aaron's 50.56 is the kind of number you frame and hang in a room you never enter again. Josef didn't need to be great, he just needed Aaron to be Aaron.
Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy handled The Bhayshul Olympics 116.5 to 78.1, and Jackson improves to 3-0 while Matt drops to 1-2 and continues his slow transformation into the league's cautionary tale.
Seven teams sit at 1-2 or worse and the playoff line is going to be an absolute bloodbath, so enjoy the calm before somebody's season ends on a Monday night flex spot.

articles.headline: The Waiver Wire Was A Ghost Town And Somehow Still Disappointing
articles.deck: Week 3 came and went with zero trades on the books and apparently zero urgency from the two teams who need it most.
body: Let's start with the bad news: this week's waiver report is basically an empty parking lot. No trades. The trades list in the league file reads like a crime scene where nothing happened. Fourteen grown men had a full week to fix their rosters and collectively decided vibes were good enough.

That would almost be fine if it weren't for Sean and Taylor sitting at 0-3 with the two worst pointsFor marks in the league, 255.2 and 268.24. Sean's Burrowed Alive scored 71.58 this week and lost by 23.18. Taylor's Victorious Secrets got run out of the building 135.44 to 107.58. Neither man touched the wire. Not a single roster move. You are 0-3, your odds sit at 10.3 and 7, and you're just going to sit there and hope Jahmyr Gibbs falls out of the sky onto your bench? He won't. He already dropped 41.4 on Andrew's team this week and Andrew is still only 1-2.
Next week Trip travels to smash Taylor again, and Ben goes to put Sean out of his misery. If either of you actually work the wire before then, congratulations, you did the bare minimum.

articles.headline: Gibbs Goes Nuclear While Everyone Else Just Watches
articles.deck: The top scorers of Week 3, owned and unowned, for better or worse.
body: Jahmyr Gibbs dropped 41.4 points on the league this week and somehow did it for a team called Bibi's Ballers 69, which means Andrew is out here winning with the wrong Falcon on the wrong roster and nobody's said a word about it. That 41.4 helped drag Bibi's Ballers past Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs 151.64 to 130.54, and Jeff can thank his own stud for keeping it that close, because Drake London went off for 28.4 and it still wasn't enough.

Meanwhile in the Game of the Week, Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 35.36 for Adam and First Down Syndrome and lost anyway, 139.78 to 135.04, because John's roster decided to just have both studs in the building. Bijan Robinson scored 35.3 and Brock Purdy threw for 31.28, and a team literally named BedBathNBIJAN22 got exactly what it paid for. Adam gets a monster game and a loss to show for it. That's fantasy football, baby, tell your therapist.

Brock Bowers chipped in 27.6 for Ben's Jackson Off in a comfortable win over Tayodin's Victorious Secrets, proof that sometimes the big performance just shows up and nobody has to suffer for it. Rare. Savor it.

articles.headline: Power Rankings Week 3: Two Unbeatens, One Bijan-Shaped Wound, And A Whole Lot Of Sadness
articles.deck: Fourteen teams, ranked from best to worst, because someone has to tell you the truth before your own therapist won't.
body: Three weeks in and the league has sorted itself into the undefeated, the delusional, and Burrowed Alive. Here's where everybody actually stands, feelings be damned.

1. 50 Shades of Zay (Trip) - 3-0, dropped a 46.02 point beatdown on Hog tied and deep fried like it owed him money, sits at 409.24 points for and 85 percent playoff odds. Clinch Watch is real and it should terrify the other 13 of you.
2. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy (Jackson) - Also 3-0, Manager of the Week, and personally responsible for making Matt's Bhayshul Olympics look like a JV scrimmage in a 38.4 point smoking.

3. BedBathNBIJAN22 (John) - Bijan Robinson went off for 35.3, Brock Purdy chipped in 31.28, and John somehow still had to sweat out a 4.74 point escape in the Game of the Week. League-best 419.56 points for and a heart condition to match.
4. Chase Browns with Downs (Jeff) - Drake London torched the field for 28.4 and Jeff still lost to Bibi's Ballers 69. That's not bad luck, Jeff, that's a defense that needs its own restraining order.

5. First Down Syndrome (Adam) - Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 35.36 and Adam still leads the entire league in points for at 420.52, yet he's 1-2 and lost the Game of the Week by 4.74. This man is scoring championships into the wrong column.
6. Jackson Off (Ben) - Brock Bowers went for 27.6 and Ben cruised past Victorious Secrets by 27.86. Comfortable win, comfortable vibes, comfortably 2-1.
7. Zyn-bo Squisher (Josef) - Beat Romo911 by 53.58 points, which is less a fantasy matchup and more a public execution.

8. Bibi's Ballers 69 (Andrew) - Jahmyr Gibbs erupted for 41.4, the single best individual performance in the league, and Andrew is still just 1-2. Imagine having that and still needing to check the standings.
9. Cook'd (Jack) - Ground out a 94.76 to 71.58 win over Burrowed Alive that nobody will remember by Tuesday, including Jack.
10. Hog tied and deep fried (Bearcat) - Got run through by Trip's 46.02 point margin and now sits 1-2 wondering what he did to deserve this life.
11. Romo911 (Aaron) - Shart of the Week. Scored 50.56, lost to Josef by 53.58, and posted the lowest score on the board this week. Aaron, buddy, that's rough sledding.
12. The Bhayshul Olympics (Matt) - Lost by 38.4 to Jackson and is now 1-2 with 32 percent playoff odds and the tag In Trouble, which feels generous.
13. Burrowed Alive (Sean) - 0-3, league-low 255.2 points for, 10.3 percent playoff odds. The name is starting to feel less like a joke and more like a prophecy.
14. Victorious Secrets (Taylor) - Also 0-3, also a Shart of the Week honoree, 7 percent playoff odds. There is nothing victorious happening here and everybody knows it, Taylor included.

articles.headline: The Trade Desk Is Closed Because Nobody Showed Up
articles.deck: Week 3 and the trade block is drier than Matt's stat line in Kansas City.
body: Nothing. Zero. The trade wire this week reads like Sean's win column. Fourteen grown men in this league and not one of you could muster the courage to pick up a phone and offer literally anything for literally anyone.

I get it. Taylor's 0-3 and probably should be dialing everybody's number right now, but instead he's sitting there at 268.24 points for the season with his hands in his pockets whistling. Sean's doing the same thing at 255.2. Two winless teams and neither of them has the stones to blow it up and try something new. That's not loyalty, fellas, that's just paralysis.

Meanwhile Matt's 1-2 with a bottom five point total and hasn't touched the block either. Adam just put up 135.04 in a loss and dropped to 1-2 despite having the second most points for in the entire league at 420.52, which should be motivating somebody to call him about literally any of his bench pieces. Nobody did.

So no grades this week. No letters, no reasoning, no nothing, because you all decided to just sit on your rosters like they're bearer bonds. Fix this. The bye weeks are coming and this league needs some chaos that isn't just Aaron losing by 53.58.
